title: First 36h launch roles and telemetry slate
body:
Purpose:
This working slate is a concise, hour-by-hour operational plan for the first 36 hours after a public rollout. Focus: short feedback loops (telemetry -> decision -> action) to protect SLOs and customer experience while we ramp.

Who should use this doc:
- Product ops lead (owner) coordinating cross-team responses
- On-call engineers (serving/runtime + infra)
- Product manager + release engineer for decision authority
- Customer success/triage for inbound customer signals

High-level objectives (first 36h):
1) Maintain p95 latency below target and error rate < 0.5% for critical routes.
2) Detect model-quality regressions on defined prompt set within 6h.
3) Ensure graceful degradation and fallback count < 1% of requests.
4) Capture all signal artifacts (samples, traces, diffs) for postmortem.

Quick glossary (short):
- SLO burn: percent of SLO budget consumed on 1h and 6h windows.
- Canary cohort: initial 1% of production traffic (if used).
- Quality probes: fixed prompt set run every 10m against serving model(s).

Roles + ownership (owner first, then backup):
- Launch commander (decision authority): Aisha Patel (backup: Marco Chen)
- Runtime on-call (latency/stability fixes): Omar Siddiqui (backup: Priya Rao)
- Model quality lead (evals & prompt set): Renee Alvarez (backup: Samira Wong)
- Customer triage (CS escalations): Hannah Lin (backup: Kyle Ortiz)
- Observability engineer (dashboards + alerts tuning): Marco Chen (backup: Luis Vega)

Shift plan (36h window):
- T+0 to T+6h: high-frequency monitoring
  - Check-ins every 30m (brief 5–10m async updates in #launch-status)
  - Live war room at T+1h (optional if any signal above threshold)
- T+6 to T+24h: steady cadence
  - Check-ins every 2h, consolidation huddles every 6h
- T+24 to T+36h: handoff to day ops
  - Final health audit at T+36h and handoff doc to product-ops backlog

KPI capture (what to record in the sheet):
- Route-level p50/p95/p99 latency (rolling 1h, 6h)
- 1h and 6h error rate (5xx + user-visible errors)
- Token cost per 1k tokens (hosted) and anomalies
- Model fallback rate and fallback latency delta
- Cache hit ratio (prefix/KV caching) and cold-start counts
- Throughput (requests/s) vs capacity thresholds
- Quality probe pass rate (per-probe, trend + example failures)
- Number of customer tickets mentioning degradation (count + severity)

Immediate alert thresholds (examples to apply in Grafana/Datadog):
- p95 latency > target * 1.4 for 3 consecutive 1m buckets -> pager to runtime on-call
- Error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> page to SRE
- Quality probe pass rate drop > 8% vs baseline in 30m -> notify model quality lead (no page unless >15%)
- Fallback rate > 1% in 10m -> page runtime + product ops

Telemetry checklist (queries / probes to have live):
- Traffic summary: requests by route, region, model variant (1h and 6h windows).
- Cost telemetry: tokens, inference worker GPU utilization, per-request cost estimate.
- Latency p50/p95/p99 by model variant and sequence length.
- Live sample stream: 1:1000 sampled responses with metadata (model id, token count, latency, cache hit).
- Quality probe runner: run canonical prompt set every 10m and push pass/fail + diff to butler. Link: CONFLUENCE-1234.
- Error trace aggregator: top 10 stack traces in last 1h with counts.

Decision ladder (fast heuristics):
1) Is the symptom user-impacting? (Yes -> escalate immediately)
2) Is this isolated to a route/region/model? (Yes -> route isolation + traffic split)
3) Can we rollback or switch to a safe variant within 5–10m? (If yes, do it and monitor)
4) If not, scale up reserved/dedicated pool (if available) and open mitigation tickets.

Runbooks (short refs, link to full playbooks):
- Quick rollback to previous model version: runbook-id: RR-42 (apply model pin -> traffic shift 90/10 -> validate 10m)
- Emergency degrade to cached responses: runbook-id: CACHE-FALLBACK-1
- Traffic quarantine for problematic user cohort: runbook-id: QUAR-7

Data capture template (paste into shared sheet quickly):
- timestamp, hour_offset, p95_latency_ms, error_rate_pct, token_cost_per_1k, fallback_pct, probe_pass_pct, notes, action_taken, owner

Communications plan:
- #launch-status channel (updates every 30m during first 6h, every 2h afterwards)
- Escalation: page runtime on-call -> call SRE lead if unresolved > 30m -> product-ops commander makes go/no-go decisions
- Customer comms: CS drafts ready-to-send templates for status page and targeted outreach (link to templates in Confluence)

Quick templates (copy into Slack):
- Short incident update: "T+{{h}}: Observed p95 latency at {{val}}ms (target {{target}}). Taking action: {{action}}. Owner: {{owner}}."
- Customer note template: "We’re aware of an incident affecting responses for [feature]. Engineers are investigating; we’ll update every 30 minutes. If you are seeing degraded responses, please reply to this thread and include a sample prompt."

Artifacts to attach to postmortem:
- 36h KPI CSV (from Data capture template)
- Live sample archive (1:1000 sampling)
- Quality probe time-series + failing examples
- Alert timeline and pager logs
- Decisions log (commander + time + rationale)

Open TODOs (pre-launch, fill these before T-0):
- [ ] Wire quality probe runner to /ops/playback with canonical set (owner: Renee)
- [ ] Create dashboard tile for fallback rate and cache hit ratio (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Preseed sample archive storage path and retention policy (owner: Observability team)
- [ ] Publish CS templates to shared folder and pre-approve language (owner: Hannah)

Notes / free-form thoughts (working):
- Consider a 2-tier alerting scheme where quality regressions only page after an immediate manual check by model quality lead; reduces false positives for noisy candidate prompts.
- We should capture model-compare diffs (new vs pinned) for top 50 failing probes automatically — useful input to product triage.
- Add a short "cost surge" alarm (token spend > forecast * 1.6) to avoid surprise infra bills in first day spikes.

Post-launch checklist (to run at T+36h):
- Compile KPI CSV and attach to launch tracker
- Confirm all high-priority incidents closed or reclassified and owners assigned
- Schedule 2-day postmortem sync (90m) with model quality, runtime, SRE, CS
- Turn this working slate into a final runbook (move to product-ops library)

If you’re on-call during the launch and see something not covered here — ping the commander and add a line to the decisions log. Keep notes terse, factual, and include timestamps.

References and links:
- Confluence: Launch telemetry patterns (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- Jira: JIRA-OPS-987 (launch checklist ticket)
summary: Working operational slate for first 36 hours after launch: roles, shifts, KPI capture fields, alert thresholds, telemetry queries, quick decision ladder, templates and postmortem artifacts. Draft form for product-ops to finalize.
